L7·N644unmasked layer
This neuron's activity centers on the internal connective/punctuation tokens that join segments of long work titles in bibliographic citations (commas and "and" between title clauses, periods ending a title, name fragments in reference lists) — with the same kind of title-linking "and"/"in" tokens in other citations driving it strongly negative, so it is essentially a citation-title-separator detector rather than a semantic feature.

L7·N7317unmasked layer
This neuron is a diffuse, low-selectivity unit that fires on ordinary English function-word/structural tokens mid-sentence — determiners, pronouns, auxiliaries and punctuation (e.g. "your", "it", "be", "The", ")", a space before a date) — with no consistent semantic theme, and is suppressed on similar function words ("may", "to", "one") and non-Latin (Bengali) byte sequences.
